neighbours.label: directional word-pieces marking motion toward a place: the split-off '-ither' of thither/whither, '-ward' and '-country' in cross-country, and the Korean directional particle -(으)로, as against the same sentences saying where something is rather than whither it goes
fire: When the storm passed, the pilgrims asked the hermit whither they should travel next, and he pointed at the hills.
"Whither are you bound at this late hour?" the innkeeper asked the tired traveller.
The knights gathered their banners and rode thither before the dawn broke over the valley.
우리는 저녁을 먹고 나서 공원으로 산책을 갔습니다.
기차가 늦어서 그는 택시를 타고 공항으로 급히 갔다.
Every winter the club organizes cross-country races through the pine forest.
The caravan turned westward once the river had been crossed.
She bought new boots for cross-country hiking in the mountains.
quiet: When the storm passed, the pilgrims asked the hermit where they should rest next, and he pointed at the hills.
"Where have you been at this late hour?" the innkeeper asked the tired traveller.
The knights gathered their banners and waited there before the dawn broke over the valley.
우리는 저녁을 먹고 나서 공원에서 산책을 했습니다.
기차가 늦어서 그는 택시를 타고 공항에서 한참 기다렸다.
Every winter the club organizes indoor races through the old sports hall.
The caravan rested quietly once the river had been crossed.
She bought new boots for long hiking in the mountains.
